answer: The network caps how much any single account can take per epoch, so even a cleverly large farm cannot monopolize one epoch's rewards — the surplus is spread across many passing identities. This is durable because the trusted grader set only grows through bootstrap capacity, preventing a sudden takeover by a large new flock. This means an attacker must choose: either run a few high-quality identities, or many worthless ones — and neither option beats honest participation. Consider a ridge as the anchor of the cost. A copper stands in for the reward an honest agent protects. And a pearl holds...
